name: github-pr-toolkit
description: Pull-request toolkit: /resolve-pr-comments works through the review threads reviewers opened (present the found threads, ask how to research them — fan out one thread-assessor subagent per thread, one at a time, or inline — on a user-selected model, then reply, fix, resolve — tracked as a task list); /code-critic authors an adversarial review of a local diff or a GitHub PR — its FIRST wizard question declares the run's outcome (fix approved findings, or only comment/report them; comment mode makes zero code changes) — across user-selected categories (general, security, design, rules-adherence, performance, tests, plus user-defined categories via the add-review-category wizard) via parallel per-category review subagents — or a single code-reviewer-all subagent covering every selected category in one dispatch, or (first-class Other answer when one is live in the repo) an agent-hierarchy durable agent reached over its gate-exempt pane.mjs transport — running on a user-selected model (session default, Opus, Sonnet, or Fable — one model across every category), with severity-triaged findings tracked as a task list, fix locally or post inline comments as one review, in a configurable feedback tone (terse / balanced / suggestion) that governs wording without touching severity or which findings are reported. One architecture: a high-reasoning orchestrator delegates ALL GitHub and outbound-git work to Haiku workers over GitHub's hosted MCP server. Delegation is enforced always, not only inside a flow: a PreToolUse guard hook denies the main agent both the GitHub MCP tools AND the gh CLI in every session (carve-outs: gh auth status, gh --version), while github-worker can read, list, search, open, and update pull requests so the delegated path is never a dead end — it will not merge one. Delegation is not a loophole in the other direction either: the same hook denies the plugin's OWN workers destructive git (reset --hard, clean, force-push, branch -D, recursive rm), and a review may remove only the worktree it created — never with --force, because needing force means there is work there a human has to rule on.

github_pat.title: GitHub Personal Access Token
github_pat.description: One PAT shared by both workers (github-worker and critic-worker), sent as a Bearer header to GitHub's hosted MCP server. Fine-grained scopes: Metadata = Read, Pull requests = Read & write (read threads/diffs, reply, resolve, post review comments), Contents = Read (code-critic's PR worktree checkout). Stored in your OS keychain — never in settings.json or a shared env var. Re-enter after plugin upgrades if GitHub access fails.

review_tone.title: Review feedback tone
review_tone.description: How /code-critic words its feedback — most visibly in the inline review comments it drafts onto a PR, which are read by someone who wasn't in the session. 'terse' = declarative and minimal, no hedging or preamble. 'balanced' = the default voice: states the problem, brief reasoning, recommended action. 'suggestion' = collaborative framing, proposals rather than verdicts. Affects WORDING ONLY: never which findings are reported, never their severity, never what the impact line says — a Critical stays Critical and still says what breaks in all three. Anything unset or unrecognized is treated as 'balanced'. Override per-run with --tone terse|balanced|suggestion, or just ask in the session.

advisor_policy.title: When reviewers consult the advisor
advisor_policy.description: The advisor is only worth its cost when it is genuinely stronger than the model asking, and its spend is the one thing the Review stats block cannot measure — so /code-critic and /resolve-pr-comments decide it rather than defaulting it on. 'auto' (default) consults only when you EXPLICITLY pick a cheaper reviewer model (Sonnet, Haiku, Fable), and withholds on Opus or a session default left alone. The test is the model you picked, not the session's own tier — a run cannot read its own tier, so a rule phrased that way could only be guessed at, and this is a cost nothing downstream can measure. 'always' consults regardless of tier. 'never' never consults. You can override any of this per-run just by asking. Anything unset or unrecognized is treated as 'auto'.

compact_checkpoint_tokens.title: Compaction checkpoint threshold (tokens)
compact_checkpoint_tokens.description: During /code-critic's issue-by-issue loop, once the conversation passes roughly this many tokens the flow offers you a compaction checkpoint before the next issue — it tells you how many issues remain and that the review state is on the task list and survives compaction. It never compacts for you; nothing can trigger /compact from inside a turn. The figure is ESTIMATED from transcript size, not measured, and is deliberately kept out of the Review stats block, which is measured-only. Default 200000. Set higher to be interrupted less, lower to be offered a checkpoint sooner.
